chunks: Announce to those who believe and have done good deeds, glad tidings of gardens under which rivers flow, and where, when they eat the fruits that grow, they will say: 'Indeed they are the same as we were given before,' so like in semblance the food would be. And they shall have fair spouses there, and live there abidingly.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rewards and characteristics of Paradise mentioned for believers in this verse?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis as a foundational description of Jannah, emphasizes the perfection of sensory and spiritual rewards for the *mu'minun*. The phrase 'mutashabihan' (resembling each other) is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi to indicate that while the fruits are familiar to earthly inhabitants, they are free from the imperfections and decay found in this world. It underscores the eternal continuity of bliss, linking the promise of Paradise directly to the combination of faith (*iman*) and righteous action (*amal al-salih*).
